In accordance with the UPRAISE objectives and FSTP framework, the selection and determination of financial support shall take account, through transparent criteria, of financial need, socio-economic circumstances, geographical/widening considerations, diversity and inclusion, as applicable. Applicants may voluntarily provide information relevant to these criteria, including socio-economic circumstances, disability or other conditions relevant to widening participation. Such information will be processed in accordance with applicable data protection rules. The specific scoring mechanism is set out in Section 11. 

7. Language requirements

Applicants must demonstrate an adequate level of proficiency in the language of instruction of the selected programme and associated UPRAISE learning activities, in accordance with the requirements established by UNINA. Where applicable, some UPRAISE activities, learning materials, seminars or international sessions may be delivered in English. 

8. Application procedure

Applications shall be submitted electronically through the procedure specified by UNINA. The call shall remain open for at least two months. The published call will specify the opening and closing dates, submission platform and contacts for administrative and technical enquiries. Applications submitted after the deadline or through channels other than those indicated in the call will not be considered.

9. Required documents

In line with the FSTP Guidelines, applicants should provide, as a minimum:

1.     Transcript of Records or equivalent academic documentation;

2.     Curriculum Vitae, maximum 3 pages, without photograph, including academic history, relevant professional experience, skills and achievements;

3.     Personal Statement/Motivation Letter, maximum 3 pages, addressing motivation for participation, relevance to UPRAISE and the proposed educational pathway, and expected academic/professional impact;

4.     copy of a valid passport or identity document;

5.     any additional documents required by UNINA to verify eligibility.

Applicants may be required to provide a declaration concerning other financial support and compliance with the applicable double-funding rules. Where relevant to the published financial-need, widening or inclusion criteria, applicants may voluntarily provide the information and supporting documentation expressly identified in the final call. UNINA will not request sensitive personal data beyond what is necessary and legally permissible for the implementation of the published criteria.

10. Eligibility check

Following the deadline, UNINA will conduct an eligibility check. Only applications satisfying the eligibility requirements, submitted on time and accompanied by the mandatory documentation will proceed to evaluation.

11. Evaluation and selection criteria

Eligible applications will be evaluated by a Selection Committee appointed by UNINA on the basis of clear, objective and transparent criteria, in accordance with Section 5.3 of the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines. Applications will be assessed on a maximum score of 100 points according to the following criteria

Criterion

Description

Weight

Academic background

Academic and Professional Background – academic records, previous qualifications, relevant professional experience and achievements, and overall preparedness for the proposed advanced digital skills learning pathway.

65 points

Motivation and proposed activity

Motivation and Expected Contribution – motivation to participate in the programme, interest in the thematic areas addressed by UPRAISE, expected contribution to the applicant’s professional and/or academic development, and potential contribution to the broader objectives and impact of the project

25 points

Curriculum Vitae

Additional Academic and Non-Academic Experience – additional relevant academic, professional and non-academic experience, skills and achievements documented in the Curriculum Vitae.

10 points



100 points

In accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines, the quality and relevance of the proposed participation in relation to the applicant’s educational and professional objectives will be considered within the above assessment criteria. Applicants must demonstrate an adequate level of proficiency in the language of instruction of the selected programme, in accordance with the requirements specified by UNINA. Diversity, equity, inclusion and widening participation considerations will be taken into account in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines. In the case of equal or comparable evaluation results, preference may be given to applicants from underrepresented groups, subject to applicable legal and institutional rules.

Applicants achieving an overall score of at least 70/100 may be considered for funding, subject to compliance with all eligibility requirements and availability of financial resources.

12. Selection committee

The Selection Committee will be appointed in accordance with UNINA rules. Its members shall act independently and impartially and comply with applicable confidentiality and conflict-of-interest requirements. The Committee will assess eligible applications against the published criteria, assign scores and establish the ranking.

13. Ranking, reserve list and award decision

Financial support will be awarded, subject to availability of funds, to the highest-ranked eligible applicants meeting the minimum threshold. A maximum of four beneficiaries will be funded under this Cycle 1 call. Eligible applicants above the threshold but not funded may be placed on a reserve list in ranking order. Where fewer than four applicants satisfy the eligibility and quality requirements, fewer than four applicants may be awarded financial support under this Call. If a selected applicant withdraws, declines the award, fails to accept it within the prescribed deadline or loses eligibility, UNINA may offer the support to the next eligible applicant on the reserve list.

14. Communication and acceptance of results

Applicants will be informed of the outcome of the selection procedure in accordance with the FSTP Guidelines. Successful applicants will receive information concerning the financial support awarded and the procedures for its acceptance. Applicants placed on the reserve list and applicants whose applications are declared ineligible or unsuccessful will be informed in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines.

15. Conditions for maintaining the support

Beneficiaries must maintain eligibility and participation in the relevant educational pathway, successfully complete the associated UPRAISE specialised learning activity in accordance with the attendance and assessment requirements set out in Section 3, comply with applicable academic and administrative requirements, provide information required for project monitoring and promptly communicate changes affecting eligibility or funding. Beneficiaries shall comply with the participation and reporting obligations established by the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines and by the relevant UNINA educational programme.

16. Fee waiver and administrative arrangements

The FSTP support under this Call is intended to cover tuition/enrolment fees through a full or partial fee waiver. No part of the financial support, including any difference between the applicable tuition/enrolment fee waiver and the maximum FSTP support of EUR 5,000 per beneficiary, will be paid directly to beneficiaries or provided in another form. The maximum support is EUR 4,000 for beneficiaries enrolled in the Master in Public Managerial Practice and EUR 5,000 for beneficiaries enrolled in the Master in Digital Transformation of Public Administration. The amount of the benefit will be individually recorded. The administrative and accounting mechanism will comply with UNINA procedures and the UPRAISE Grant Agreement.

17. Double funding

Financial support awarded under this Call shall comply with the applicable rules on double funding, in accordance with the UPRAISE Grant Agreement and FSTP Guidelines.

18. Monitoring, records and audits

UNINA will retain the documentation required to ensure an adequate audit trail for publication, applications, eligibility checks, evaluation, selection, award and implementation. 

19. Redress procedure

A redress procedure will be provided in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines and the applicable UNINA procedures.

20. Data protection 

Personal data submitted in connection with this Call will be processed in accordance with the applicable data protection legislation and the relevant University of Napoli Federico II privacy notice.

21. Publication and visibility

Following the required review and confirmation procedure, the call will be published simultaneously through the channels required by the UPRAISE/HaDEA implementation arrangements, including the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, the Digital Skills and Jobs Platform (DSJP), the UPRAISE project website and the institutional website of the University of Napoli Federico II. The call will remain open for at least two months. The English version will be the reference version; an Italian version may also be made available.

22. Disclaimer

This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by UPRAISE. Any financial support awarded under this call will be granted directly by UPRAISE to the successful applicants, in its own name and under its sole responsibility. UPRAISE's own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants that will receive the said financial support. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim to increase the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of UPRAISE.

description:
The UPRAISE project, co-funded by the European Union under the Digital Europe Programme, strengthens Europe's advanced digital skills capacity in innovation, entrepreneurship and Virtual Worlds technologies. Through its Financial Support to Third Parties scheme, the University of Patras invites eligible students to apply for financial support for outgoing international learning and mobility activities connected with UPRAISE.

The call supports international academic collaboration, practical skills acquisition, employability and participation in advanced digital education. Applications linked to the University of Patras application areas within UPRAISE are particularly encouraged: healthcare, education and creativity, and food-related applications of advanced digital and Virtual Worlds technologies.

Available grants and mobility streams: 3

Eligible Costs: Enrolment fee; travel and accommodation; living expenses

Max Support per mobility stream: EUR 5,000

The maximum support is a ceiling. The final amount awarded may be lower, depending on the approved activity, eligible costs, available complementary funding, and University of Patras procedures. Use of a reserve list or any reallocation affecting this call must be formally documented and remain within the approved Cycle 1 FSTP budget.

Email: dtsolis@upatras.gr, Telephone: +302610996900

furtherInformation:
Eligible applicants

  1. Be formally enrolled at the University of Patras in a doctoral, postgraduate or undergraduate program appropriate to the selected mobility stream.
  2. Meet the academic and administrative requirements of the proposed host institution, program, summer/winter school, internship or learning activity.
  3. Have an academic profile and proposed activity aligned with UPRAISE themes, such as Virtual Worlds, XR, AI, digital twins, advanced digital innovation, or relevant applications in healthcare, education and creativity, and food.
  4. Have adequate command of English, normally at least B2 level, or the language required by the host activity.
  5. Hold the nationality of an EU Member State or another country eligible under the Digital Europe Program, in accordance with the applicable call rules.
  6. Be able to complete the proposed activity within the eligibility period established in the award documentation.


Eligible activities and costs

Financial support may cover only the cost categories specified below and directly related to the approved mobility activity:

  1. Enrolment or participation fees for an eligible program, module, summer/winter school or other approved learning activity.
  2. Travel and accommodation costs.
  3. Living expenses and subsistence during the approved mobility period, including local transport where permitted by institutional rules.

Double funding of the same expense is strictly prohibited. The grant may be combined with another compatible source, such as Erasmus+, only where the funding sources cover different eligible costs and all applicable institutional rules are respected.


Inclusion and prioritisation

The prioritisation categories are applied only after eligibility and academic qualification have been established. They are not mutually exclusive and will support a balanced cohort while preserving merit-based selection. .

  1. Women and other genders underrepresented in ICT-related fields.
  2. Applicants from low socio-economic backgrounds or experiencing significant financial hardship.
  3. Applicants with disabilities and applicants belonging to minority, migrant, refugee or other vulnerable groups.
  4. Applicants from countries or regions with lower advanced digital skills capacity.
  5. Applicants who belong to more than one priority category or who contribute to the overall balance of the selected cohort.

Information relating to priority categories is voluntary, confidential and processed only where necessary under applicable data protection rules. Applicants who wish to be considered under a priority category may provide only the minimum information needed to establish that category: optional gender self-identification; a brief statement of low socio-economic background or significant financial hardship, with income-related or financial-aid evidence where available and permitted under University procedures; a self-declaration that disability, minority, migrant, refugee or other vulnerable-group status applies, with non-diagnostic official confirmation only where strictly necessary; and country or region of residence, origin or prior study for geographical widening. Applicants may also indicate that more than one priority category applies. Applicants are not required to disclose medical diagnoses, detailed health information, ethnicity, religion or other sensitive details beyond what is necessary to establish the claimed category. Where official evidence is unavailable or requesting it would be inappropriate, self-declarations may be accepted in accordance with University procedures and applicable data protection rules. If two or more applicants have the same final score, the Selection Committee may use the above factors, financial need and the overall cohort balance as tie-breakers and must document the rationale.


Award, payment and obligations

  1. All applicants will be informed of the outcome. Successful applicants must accept the award within the period stated in the notification.
  2. Before payment, selected applicants may be required to sign a grant agreement, learning agreement, declaration of honour, double-funding declaration and other University of Patras documents.
  3. Recipients must implement the approved activity, provide evidence of participation and eligible expenditure where requested, and cooperate with monitoring, reporting, audits and checks.
  4. Withdrawal or cancellation must be communicated promptly in writing. Financial support already received may have to be reimbursed when the activity is not implemented or eligibility conditions are not fulfilled.
  5. The selected activity should be academically recognised through ECTS or another appropriate certification where applicable, according to the rules of the University of Patras and the host institution.


Redress procedure

Applicants may request a review only in relation to an alleged procedural or administrative error affecting the evaluation. A redress request may not challenge the academic judgement of evaluators unless a procedural irregularity may have influenced the result. Requests must be submitted to dtsolis@upatras.gr within 10 calendar days of notification.


Data protection and confidentiality

The University of Patras acts as Data Controller for personal data processed in connection with this call. Personal data will be used only for application management, evaluation, award administration, project monitoring, reporting, audit and compliance purposes under Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and applicable national legislation. Applicants will receive or be directed to the relevant University of Patras privacy notice before submission.


Disclaimer

This call, as well as the financial support that will be provided through it, is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by UPRAISE. Any financial support awarded under this call will be granted directly by UPRAISE to the successful applicants, in its own name and under its sole responsibility. UPRAISE's responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants. Publication of this call on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is solely for information purposes and to increase visibility. Such publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any waiver of UPRAISE's responsibility.

The Call has 5 distinct cut-off dates. All submitted applications by each deadline will be evaluated jointly and awarded until funding resources are available. The AI-SECRETT consortium reserves the right of integrating the funding budget with an extra allocation, up to twice the initially allocated amount. A same natural person can apply multiple times at different cut-off dates but can receive the financial benefits of this Call only once.

Applications will only be possible electronically and exclusively managed through the GoodGrantsTM platform (https://aisecrett.grantplatform.com/) by filling in a form and attaching the required documentation.

Evaluation of received applications will be done by a special committee established at the Funding Body, Universidad de Valencia (UVEG). Each application will be evaluated from the perspectives of admissibility, eligibility, and merit.

Admissibility conditions will be that an electronic application has been received on or before the latest cut-off date, completed in all its parts, and with all required attachments, exclusively through the GoodGrantsTM platform. Incomplete applications or submitted by other means will be discarded and proposed for resubmission at the next cut-off date.

To pass the admissibility check, all applicants must submit at least:

-      A signed application form;

-      Their CV in Europass format (see https://europass.europa.eu/en/create-europass-cv);

-      A motivation letter (explicitly stating employment status and financial need);

-      Any documentation supporting disadvantaged background and/or priority categories (where applicable);

-      Signed declarations (no conflict of interest, double funding, etc.) using the templates available on the GoodGrantsTM platform;

-      A proof of enrolment or acceptance in the AI-SECRETT master’s programme, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date;

-      A proof of enrolment or acceptance in at least one extracurricular activity of the AI-SECRETT project, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date; and

-      An indicative cost breakdown (travel, accommodation, registration/participation fees, other costs).

All the above documentation must be provided in English language. Unofficial translations are allowed in case of submission of documents that are natively not in English, but the applicant will take the risk and bear the consequences of any misinterpretation during the evaluation process.

Eligibility conditions will be that

-      The applicants must be natural persons and nationals of an eligible country for the Call (see Further information below);

-      They must not be subject to restrictive measures or other disqualifying conditions according to the EU or national legislation in their country;

-      They cannot receive double funding for the same operation;

-      They must not be in a situation of conflict of interest with UVEG or any other AI-SECRETT partner.

Eligible applications received until the same cut-off date will be scored using the following criteria (max. 100 points):

Criterion

Description

Max score

Excellence and relevance

Academic/professional background and fit with AI‑SECRETT vertical industries (*)

30

Motivation and expected impact

Learning objectives, career impact, clarity of plan

25

Financial need

Economic situation and justification of requested support

25

European added value

Cross‑border dimension, diversity contribution

20

(*) Agri-Food, Cultural and Creative Industries, Energy and Environment, Housing, Manufacturing, Mobility and Transport, and Non-Touristic Services.

No minimum thresholds or weighting will be applied. In case of equal scores, the following priority rules will be adopted, in the same order:

  1. Applicants enrolled in more than one extracurricular activity.
  2. Applicants from countries not full members of the AI‑SECRETT consortium.
  3. Applicants from regions with average income below 75% of the EU average.
  4. Female applicants (if merit equivalent).

The maximum financial support per beneficiary is:

EUR 5 000 (five thousand Euros / 00)

The awarded amount is calculated on the basis of:

-      Actual and justified travel costs,

-      Actual and justified accommodation costs,

-      Actual and documented registration/participation fees,

-      Actual, justified and documented other costs.

as reported in the indicative cost breakdown (see above). The Selection Committee may cap specific cost items if considered excessive or not in line with typical market prices for the location and period.

The awarded amount will be adjusted to the recipient’s country of origin following the latest adjustment coefficients of the Marie Skłodowska Curie actions available (see e.g. https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/horizon/wp-call/2023-2024/wp-2-msca-actions_horizon-2023-2024_en.pdf).

Eligible expenses are those realised after the date of submission of the respective application.

The scheme reimburses up to 50% of total eligible costs, within the 5 000 EUR cap, so that the minimum number of supported beneficiaries with available resources (equally distributed across two yearly editions of this Call) will be at least 240.

The procedure follows the principles of:

  1. transparency,
  2. equal treatment,
  3. confidentiality,
  4. absence of conflict of interest.

Admissibility and eligibility checks precede scoring; only eligible applications will be scored.

Eligible proposals are ranked by total score within the available budget.

The final award decision is endorsed by UVEG. All applicants will receive a written justification for the decision, with terms to appeal.

Selected beneficiaries will be requested to sign a Financial Support Agreement (see text here: https://aisecrett.eu/bid-to-our-call/FSA) specifying the supported activity, eligible costs, maximum amount, payment schedule and reporting obligations.

Failure to sign within the indicated timeframe may lead to loss of the grant by the autonomous decision of UVEG.

Payments will be made by UVEG, normally after participation in the activity and approval of the beneficiary report and cost statement. Details are provided in the individual Financial Support Agreement (including e.g. the possibility of small prefinancing in justified cases).

Inclusion and prioritisation

The prioritisation categories are applied only after eligibility and academic qualification have been established. They are not mutually exclusive and will support a balanced cohort while preserving merit-based selection. .

  1. Women and other genders underrepresented in ICT-related fields.
  2. Applicants from low socio-economic backgrounds or experiencing significant financial hardship.
  3. Applicants with disabilities and applicants belonging to minority, migrant, refugee or other vulnerable groups.
  4. Applicants from countries or regions with lower advanced digital skills capacity.
  5. Applicants who belong to more than one priority category or who contribute to the overall balance of the selected cohort.

Information relating to priority categories is voluntary, confidential and processed only where necessary under applicable data protection rules. Applicants who wish to be considered under a priority category may provide only the minimum information needed to establish that category: optional gender self-identification; a brief statement of low socio-economic background or significant financial hardship, with income-related or financial-aid evidence where available and permitted under University procedures; a self-declaration that disability, minority, migrant, refugee or other vulnerable-group status applies, with non-diagnostic official confirmation only where strictly necessary; and country or region of residence, origin or prior study for geographical widening. Applicants may also indicate that more than one priority category applies. Applicants are not required to disclose medical diagnoses, detailed health information, ethnicity, religion or other sensitive details beyond what is necessary to establish the claimed category. Where official evidence is unavailable or requesting it would be inappropriate, self-declarations may be accepted in accordance with University procedures and applicable data protection rules. If two or more applicants have the same final score, the Selection Committee may use the above factors, financial need and the overall cohort balance as tie-breakers and must document the rationale.

Award, payment and obligations

  1. All applicants will be informed of the outcome. Successful applicants must accept the award within the period stated in the notification.
  2. Before payment, selected applicants may be required to sign a grant agreement, learning agreement, declaration of honour, double-funding declaration and other University of Patras documents.
  3. Recipients must implement the approved activity, provide evidence of participation and eligible expenditure where requested, and cooperate with monitoring, reporting, audits and checks.
  4. Withdrawal or cancellation must be communicated promptly in writing. Financial support already received may have to be reimbursed when the activity is not implemented or eligibility conditions are not fulfilled.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Proposal submission:

All proposals shall be submitted at: https://share.hsforms.com/133VDDomZReqeyGTex0VYRwf4os

Proposal template and supporting documents:

The proposal template and supporting documents are available at: https://www.llm-bridge.eu/open-calls-2/

Evaluation process:

Eligible proposals will be evaluated by independent external experts, appointed by the LLM-BRIDGE Consortium, to ensure objectivity and impartiality.

Each proposal will be assessed by at least two experts using the criteria and scoring system defined in the Evaluation Criteria.

Applicants will be notified of the evaluation results within four weeks after completion of the panel ranking.

Each applicant will receive an Evaluation Summary Report (ESR) containing individual scores, comments, and the final consensus assessment.

The successful applicant will be invited to sign a Financial Support Agreement with 28DIGITAL on behalf of the LLM-BRIDGE Consortium.

Evaluation criteria:

The evaluation is based on the following criteria, each with a maximum score and a minimum threshold:

Relevance (maximum score: 10; threshold: 6): Assessment of how well the proposal aligns with the objectives of LLM-BRIDGE, including its capacity to support early-stage Generative AI startups and contribute to European GenAI strategic goals.

Track record (maximum score: 8; threshold: 5): Evaluation of the applicant’s proven experience in incubating and scaling AI or deep-tech ventures, with demonstrated results in terms of startup growth and innovation.

Networks and access (maximum score: 8; threshold: 5): Consideration of the ability to provide startups with access to mentors, investors, and strategic industry partners that can strengthen their market positioning and growth potential.

Adaptability (maximum score: 6; threshold: 4): Evidence of flexibility and capacity to respond to emerging technological and market needs, particularly in the rapidly evolving Generative AI sector.

Monitoring framework (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Quality and clarity of the proposed processes and documentation for monitoring and reporting, including well-defined metrics to track startup progress and overall programme performance.

Cost effectiveness (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Adequacy and justification of the proposed budget, demonstrating efficient use of resources and value for money.

Each criterion is scored from 0 up to its maximum (10, 8, 6 or 5). Proposals are evaluated according to six qualitative levels.

Not addressed (score 0 in all scales): The proposal fails to address the criterion or cannot be assessed.

Poor (score 1–2 out of 10, 1–2 out of 8, or 1 out of 5/6): The proposal shows serious weaknesses or lacks the required level of detail.

Fair (score 3–4 out of 10, 3–4 out of 8, or 2 out of 5/6): Some strengths are present, but significant weaknesses remain.

Good – threshold level (score 5–6 out of 10, 5 out of 8, or 3–4 out of 5/6): The criterion is adequately addressed, though moderate weaknesses are observed.

Very good (score 7–8 out of 10, 6–7 out of 8, or 4–5 out of 5/6): The criterion is well addressed, with only minor shortcomings.

Excellent (score 9–10 out of 10, 8 out of 8, or 5–6 out of 5/6): The criterion is fully addressed, demonstrating outstanding quality with no or only negligible weaknesses.

Threshold per criterion: 3 to 6 points. Overall minimum score: 26 points (out of 42). Maximum total score: 42 points. Proposals failing to reach the threshold in any criterion or the overall minimum score will not be considered for funding.
description:
The Venture Incubation Programme (VIP) serves as an instrument to strengthening incubation capacity in Europe to support early-stage GenAI ventures as well as to:

  1. Accelerate the commercialisation of LLM technologies, providing mentoring, access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources, data infrastructures, and regulatory guidance.
  2. Promote responsible AI innovation, aligned with the AI Act, Data Act, GDPR, and the EU’s Digital Decade Targets.
  3. Foster cross-border collaboration, knowledge sharing, and participation of underrepresented regions and groups in the European AI ecosystem.


Through this call, LLM-BRIDGE seeks to identify and support one high-quality, EU-based incubator capable of supporting startups in the transforming of early-stage GenAI ideas into viable, scalable, and ethically compliant ventures that may be eligible to apply for the future Long Jump and European Grand Challenges. Participating in the VIP provides an opportunity for a leading incubator to position itself at the forefront of Europe’s generative AI revolution. This collaboration offers strategic, reputational, and operational advantages, aligning the incubator with a pan-European initiative that seeks to redefine the future of AI-driven innovation and technological leadership. 

The VIP programme will select one incubator to run a 12-week VIP cohort across Europe, which will:

  1. Deliver structured training and mentoring to 30 startups.
  2. Provide and facilitate access to technical expertise and AI infrastructures.
  3. Monitor and report progress using standardised KPIs defined in the Annex I. 
  4. Contribute to the overall impact of LLM-BRIDGE and the European GenAI innovation ecosystem.

The selected incubator will gain direct access to a carefully selected pipeline of high-potential GenAI startups from across Europe, allowing it to deepen its expertise in nurturing deep-tech ventures with the potential to drive the next wave of generative AI solutions. Such engagement not only enhances the incubators reputation as a leading enabler of cutting-edge innovation but also strengthens its market position within the highly competitive AI ecosystem.

beneficiaryAdministration: Official AENAON Open Call submission portal, accessible through the Open Call section of the AENAON website: https://aenaon-project.eu/ Submissions platform: https://aenaon.grantplatform.com/
description:
Basic information

AENAON implements two competitive Open Call rounds through its Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) scheme. The Open Calls aim to maximise the uptake, integration, testing and validation of AENAON technologies and services, including the Federated Digital Twin-based Cyber Range Platform, cybersecurity training capabilities and cybersecurity preparedness services, in realistic offshore wind and related critical-infrastructure environments.

The Open Calls are designed to engage SMEs and start-ups, large enterprises and technology providers, research organisations and universities, cybersecurity service and technology providers, offshore wind operators, manufacturers and supply-chain actors, energy and critical-infrastructure stakeholders, and other relevant innovation actors. Supported third-party projects are expected to contribute practical use cases, validation evidence, technical feedback and sector-relevant results that strengthen the cybersecurity and resilience of the offshore wind ecosystem.

Open Call 1 focuses on the initial validation, integration and testing of AENAON technologies and services in realistic environments. Activities may include the development and validation of sector-specific cybersecurity scenarios, identification and assessment of offshore-wind-relevant vulnerabilities, integration with simulation and cyber range environments, cybersecurity testing and training activities, and validation of cybersecurity tools, services and preparedness capabilities.

Open Call 1 sub-projects are expected to have an implementation period of 8 months, with clearly defined tasks, milestones, deliverables, KPIs and acceptance evidence.

Applicants may propose activities related to cybersecurity testing and validation, cyber range training and scenario-based exercises, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, threat and risk assessment, risk monitoring, cyberattack management, digital twin-based validation and integration, or other cybersecurity resilience use cases that are demonstrably aligned with the objectives and technical capabilities of AENAON.

Budget

The total AENAON FSTP budget is €4,100,000.

The indicative allocation is:

  1. €2,100,000 for Open Call 1
  2. €2,000,000 for Open Call 2

Any amount not committed under Open Call 1 may be reallocated to Open Call 2, subject to budget availability, the applicable Open Call rules and the principles of transparency, equal treatment and sound financial management.

Funding Constraints

AENAON will provide sub-grants under two Open Calls (Open Call 1 and 2), with a total FSTP allocation of €4,100,000. In line with the call topic, the scheme derogates from the €60k ceiling, allowing up to €100,000 per individual third party (only in the case of offshore wind farm operators and manufacturers, which are considered large critical infrastructures/ operators of essential services) and up to €150,000 per action (in case of small consortia).

Example 1 — SME A, Open Call 1

  1. Entity A is a generic SME, applicable ceiling: €60,000
  2. Funding requested/awarded in Open Call 1: €55,000
  3. Result: Eligible (Remaining funding capacity for Open Call 2 under AENAON: €5,000, if applicable)

Example 2 — Offshore wind-farm operator B, Open Call 1

  1. Entity B is an offshore wind-farm operator and therefore benefits from the derogated ceiling; applicable ceiling: €100,000
  2. Funding awarded in Open Call 1: €87,000
  3. Result: Eligible (Remaining funding capacity for Open Call 2: €13,000, if applicable)

Example 3 — Small consortium B + C, Open Call 2

  1. In Open Call 2, B and C form a small consortium. B = offshore wind-farm operator/manufacturer, and C = SME, thus, maximum funding per consortium action: €150,000.
  2. However, the individual ceilings must also be respected. Since B already received €87,000 in Open Call 1, B can receive only €100,000 − €87,000 = €13,000
  3. C has received no previous AENAON funding. Therefore, C can receive up to €60,000
  4. The total maximum eligible AENAON funding for the consortium (B+C) in Open Call 2 is therefore €73,000 (B up to €13,000, C up to €60,000)
  5. Consortium action (budget requested): €73k < €150k maximum per action

The final lump-sum amount awarded to each selected third-party beneficiary will be fixed at the contracting stage through a needs-based, auditable right-sizing process, taking into account the proposed activities, technical complexity, budget needs, expected contribution to AENAON objectives, evaluation outcome, milestones, deliverables, and acceptance criteria.

Payment Schedule

AENAON applies a staged payment model of 30% – 40% – 30%:

  1. 30% initial payment upon signature of the Sub-Grant Agreement and completion of onboarding requirements
  2. 40% interim payment following successful completion of the mid-term review and acceptance of required interim reports, deliverables and supporting evidence
  3. 30% final payment following completion of the action and acceptance of the final report, final deliverables, performance evidence and required outputs

Payments are conditional upon the satisfactory achievement of agreed milestones, deliverables and acceptance criteria. Payments may be suspended, reduced or recovered in cases of non-performance, breach of contractual obligations, false declarations, conflict of interest, ineligible activities or serious non-compliance with reporting, ethics, GDPR, visibility or audit requirements.

furtherInformation:
The call is open to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises registered in Finland.

Financial support may be provided for projects that aim to promote market readiness and commercialisation of innovative cybersecurity solutions. Financial support may be granted for example piloting, optimizing and other development measures supporting market readiness of the solution, as well as for other measures promoting the commercialization, market entry, uptake and determining the preconditions for internationalisation of a product or service.

Only innovative cybersecurity solutions with a high technological readiness level (TRL) shall be financed. Marketing actions, other sales promotion actions or export aid or aid contingent upon the use of domestic goods or services over imported one shall not be financed.

Financial support of a minimum of EUR 10,000 and a maximum of EUR 100,000 may be granted per project. There is a 30 % self-financing (co-funding) requirement per project. 70 % of the financial support is paid after the administrative funding decision and 30 % after the project report and actually incurred costs have been approved by the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom. 

You can find more information about the terms and conditions on the NCC-FI website: https://www.kyberturvallisuuskeskus.fi/en/our-activities/national-coordination-centre-cyber-security-research-development-and-innovation

The project proposal will be submitted by the applicant via the application form attached to this call for proposals. The proposal will include the mandatory annexes and any other annexes that the applicants decide to attach in order to demonstrate the eligibility, quality and applicability of the results, the suitability of the proposed mechanism for their application in the context of sustainability, or other parameters of the project.

For each project, a member of the NCC-CZ Council will be appointed by the NCC-CZ Council to manage the evaluation process, based on the submission and the sectoral focus of the project. As part of the evaluation, the NCC-CZ administrators will assess the formal compliance of the submitted project proposal with the requirements of the call and will carry out an assessment of the acceptability of the project in terms of the substantive requirements for projects. An independent evaluators will assess the quality and compliance with the material requirements of the projects in accordance with the Terms of Reference of the NCC-CZ and this call.

Further information available on: Národní úřad pro kybernetickou a informační bezpečnost - Výzvy
description:
The aim of the call is to support the creation, development and practical validation of scalable solutions that address the documented needs of the Czech cybersecurity ecosystem. Supported projects must combine design or development, at least one pilot deployment or practical validation, evaluation of results and preparation for further use. The call is focused on three thematic areas:

The call is focused on three main thematic pillars:

• Scalable solutions for the resilience of small and medium-sized enterprises: new or significantly expanded services and tools to protect small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), self-assessment, prioritisation of measures and sector- specific implementation packages.

• Implementation tools and services for compliance readiness, management and risk management: practical solutions for NIS2, CRA, DORA, supply chain security, cybersecurity management, record-keeping, reporting, secure development, SBOM and vulnerability management.

• Services and technical solutions for incident preparedness, response and recovery: standardised services, sector-specific scenarios, exercise packages and tools for recovery testing, record-keeping, escalation and reporting.

Support will be given primarily to projects that aim to deliver solutions with a measurable impact on a wider target group. Analyses alone, general training or documentation without implementation and validation activities are not a priority. Implementation by individual organisations is eligible primarily as a means of piloting the transferability and wider applicability of the results.

furtherInformation:
In accordance with the programme’s terms and conditions, the maximum amount of financial support is €100,000 and the minimum amount is €60,000 (in the form of a grant),depending on the current exchange rate of the Czech koruna. Projects will be funded at a rate of 50% of eligible costs, which means that the beneficiary will receive funding amounting to one half of the eligible costs incurred during the implementation of the project and substantiated in accordance with the established rules. The funding awarded to a project may be lower than the amount that was requested in the application. The decision on the final amount of support granted will depend on the quality of the project application, the consistency of the expected results with the proposed budget, and the structure of the individual planned costs.

Beneficiaries will be required to regularly provide evidence of actual expenditure incurred in connection with the implementation of the project. Details regarding the frequency and format of reporting will be specified in the grant agreement. Applicants must ensure that the project proposal meets the conditions designed to prevent the project funding from resulting in unauthorised indirect state aid within the meaning of relevant European legislation, or from leading to double funding.

The following types of organisations are eligible to participate in this call and meet the criteria set out in the EU Digital Europe programme:

• Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

• Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) that demonstrate professional competence and the ability to produce and practically validate an output in line with the objectives of the call.

• Academic and research institutions are eligible only as members of a consortium that includes at least one small or medium-sized enterprise. They may not submit an application on their own.

Consortia may combine the above-mentioned entities. The application must specify the actual roles, responsibilities and budgets of the members; a formal partnership without evidence of added value is not sufficient.

results.summary: Open Call for Cutting-Edge Defence Solutions
results.content: Open Call for Cutting-Edge Defence Solutions

beneficiaryAdministration:
The BattleVerse project, a European Defence Fund Development Action co-funded under grant agreement No 101224034, foresees the provision of Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP), also referred to as Cascade Funding, to support innovative experiments contributing to the objectives of the project.

The BattleVerse 1st Open Call is designed to support innovative experiments contributing to the development and validation of advanced technologies for mission planning, simulation, training and execution in defence-related environments. The Open Call primarily targets SMEs, including start-ups, and will provide selected beneficiaries with financial support to implement experiments over a period of six months.

The Open Call covers three technical topics designed to advance next-generation defence simulation capabilities. Applicants are invited to propose innovative solutions in AI-enabled decision support (including Machine Learning, LLMs, strategic decision-making and human-in-the-loop AI), advanced modelling and simulation (including MSaaS, Digital Twins and multi-domain simulation environments), or autonomous defence systems (including unmanned vehicles, distributed AI and swarm operations).

Proposal applications must be submitted exclusively via the BattleVerse Submission Portal.

Experiments may be implemented by a single SME or start-up, or by an eligible consortium of up to three beneficiaries. Participation of entities other than SMEs, including RTOs and academic institutions, may only be accepted where no suitable SME is available to provide the specific capacity or expertise required for the successful implementation of the experiment, and such participation must be duly justified in the proposal.

The proposal must be written in English in all mandatory parts to be eligible. The project description shall not exceed 15 pages as indicated in the Proposal Template. Only a proposal included in the Proposal Template will be reviewed by Evaluators. The evaluation will be performed per topics. Applications submitted by email, post, or any means other than the one described above will not be considered.

The assessment of the Call will follow transparent evaluation criteria, lump-sum funding modalities, and strict governance procedures in full compliance with the corresponding EDF's Model Grant Agreement.

The eligibility criteria applicable to the BattleVerse 1st Open Call reflect the relevant requirements of the European Defence Fund and the specific conditions established for Financial Support to Third Parties. To be eligible, applicants must:

  1. Be a legal private entity qualifying as Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise as defined by the European Commission. Entities other than SMEs may participate only in duly justified cases where the specific capacity or expertise required for the experiment cannot be provided by an available eligible SME.
  2. Applicants must be legal entities established in any of the countries eligible for this open call: A EU27 Member State or Norway or Ukraine. This follows country eligibility criteria under the EDF as well as the Commission Implementing Decision of 29 January 2025 (C(2025) 568 final
  3. EDF-funded activities are subject to specific ownership and control requirements in accordance with Article 9 EDF Regulation. To be eligible for this Call, entities must be established in an EU Member State, Norway or Ukraine. Applicants controlled by an entity from a non-eligible country will be excluded.
  4. Applicants must comply with all eligibility criteria defined in this Guide for Applicants, including requirements related to geographical scope, ownership control, security requirements, conflict of interest and data protection. These conditions are aligned with the applicable rules of the European Defence Fund, tailored to the reality of financial support to third parties.
  5. Applicants must have the know-how, qualifications and resources to successfully implement the projects and contribute their share (including sufficient experience in projects of comparable size and nature).
  6. Applicants to this Call must submit the Ownership Control Declaration.
  7. Comply with ethics requirements as defined in Article 7 of EDF Regulation.
  8. Comply with security requirements of the Call.
  9. Comply with financial capacity requirements of the Call.
  10. Comply with any other specificity of the Call.
  11. Not have any conflict of interest with BattleVerse consortium partners.
description:
The BattleVerse 1st Open Call aims to support the development and validation of innovative technological solutions that contribute to advanced mission planning, simulation, training and execution in defence related environments. Selected applicants will implement a six-month experiment, developing and demonstrating their proposed solution and assessing its potential contribution to the BattleVerse ecosystem.

Proposals shall address one of the following three technical topics:

Topic 1: LLMs for strategic decision-making, symbolic reasoning, game theory and planning under uncertainty. Experiments under this topic will explore the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI-based approaches to support strategic decision-making and mission planning, including symbolic reasoning, game-theoretic modelling, planning under uncertainty and human-in-the-loop approaches.

Topic 2: Multi-physics simulation capabilities for multi-domain defence environments. Experiments selected under this topic should explore and demonstrate simulation approaches capable of modelling complex operational environments and interactions across multiple warfare domains.

Topic 3: Distributed AI for autonomous systems (UxVs) with for coordinated swarm operations. Experiments selected under this topic should explore and demonstrate how autonomous systems powered by machine learning and distributed AI can support coordinated multi-UxV operations in complex operational environments.

Across the three topics, proposed experiments should demonstrate a clear technological contribution, a credible implementation approach and the potential to advance the capabilities of the BattleVerse simulation environment. Experiments are expected to achieve at least TRL 5 by the end of the six-month implementation period.

Selected beneficiaries will also have access to targeted coaching and guidance activities provided by the BattleVerse consortium. These activities will support applicants in addressing relevant technical challenges related to the development, integration, testing and validation of their solutions. The selected beneficiaries will remain fully responsible for the implementation and delivery of their experiments.

title: Missiles, ammunition and bombs
callTitle: 1st call for proposals for industrial reinforcement actions under the Ukraine Support Instrument
descriptionByte:
Expected Impact:

Projects are expected to deliver results aligned with the expected results set out in this call topic and to evidence their contribution through dedicated KPIs defined in the proposal.

Expected results include:

• demonstrable and sustainable increase in production capacity for the targeted ammunition, bombs and missiles production lines, enabled by operational joint filling plants and production lines;

• measurable reduction of production lead time from order/production decision to delivery in UA;

• improved timely availability and supply of defence products for UA, including increased delivery reliability and readiness of production lines;

• effective cross-border cooperation between UA and EU that enables production ramp-up, qualification, integration and sustainment.

Proposals shall define, baseline and track KPIs such as: filling throughput (e.g., units/month or tonnes/month as applicable), time-to-rate, lead-time reduction, line availability/uptime, acceptance/qualification output, qualified output delivered in UA, workforce trained where relevant, and indicators evidencing risk mitigation (e.g., safety performance and compliance readiness, supply robustness and maintainability readiness).

Objective:

This topic aims to reinforce missiles, ammunition and bombs readiness and their sovereign component base by enabling the rapid industrial reinforcement of Member States and Ukraine for key defence product (including subcomponents) production lines:

• air defence (conventional and non-conventional) missiles and ammunition (including counter-UxS systems);

• deep strike capabilities (including long-range missiles);

• rockets, (smart) bombs and loitering munitions.

Actions shall be aligned with the objectives, scope and priorities of this call topic, and implemented as Ira under USI in line with Regulation (EU) 2025/2643. Proposals are expected to ensure timely availability and supply of defence products for Ukraine, by scaling production capacity and industrial readiness for cross-border (EU-UA) industrial set-up in the form of:

• joint filling plants and production lines;

• reinforcement of specific production capacity and enablement capacity (including integration and validation/testing of alternative control and navigation approaches, production/integration of sensing and effector modules, multi-sensor fusion integration, and dedicated assembly/test capacity/production planning to sustain high monthly volumes, as applicable);

• scale-up of UA systems and ready-to-use production lines (including rapid-cycle modular assembly and re-configuration capacity to adapt to fast-evolving threats and mission profiles);

• MaaS (Manufacturing as a Service) (including rapid small-batch production, fast line changeover, and scalable assembly/test capacity for attritable UxS output);

• dual-use heavy industry conversion options for defence surge (including surge assembly/integration, test, packaging, and supporting infrastructure as applicable).

Applicants may include an optional dedicated Work Package (WP) implementing a supporting action as defined in Article 13(d) of Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, to reinforce the physical and cyber protection of the production capacity targeted by the action, including on security against UxS/drone-enabled threats. The objective is to reduce the risk of disruption, sabotage or interference affecting production continuity, ramp-up and deliveries, complementing the proposal’s overall risk-management approach (notably safety, supply-chain and obsolescence, industrialisation/integration, and maintainability risks) and supporting the achievement of the industrial KPIs set for lead time and capacity.

Scope:

Proposals shall implement Industrial Reinforcement Actions, in line with Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, targeting the specific defence product and production capacities listed under “Objectives pursued”.

Proposals shall demonstrate the criticality of the targeted defence product (including subcomponents) and justify the urgency of reinforcing their availability and security of supply through the proposed industrial reinforcement activities.

Proposals shall include a risk-management approach commensurate with industrial ramp-up in UA (including safety and regulatory compliance for energetic materials and filling activities, supply-chain and obsolescence, industrialisation/integration, maintainability, and operational constraints), and explain how risks are mitigated to ensure timely availability and supply of defence products in UA.

Activities linked to the physical and cyber protection WP may include expert threat assessment, procurement, installation and initial integration of proportionate solutions as well as efforts to connect to a national or European security system for: (i) counter-UxS site protection measures (detection/alerting and other authorised protective measures), and/or (ii) cyber protection measures of production-relevant networks and systems (including monitoring, hardening and secure access) which includes obtaining the European Union Cybersecurity Certification (EUCC) schemes for products used in the IRA activity, as well as acceptance testing and operational set-up necessary for effective deployment, in order to work towards compliance with the NIS2 Directive, where applicable, and alignment with standards such as ISO/IEC 27001 and IEC 62443.

Actions shall not have started before 5 March 2024 and shall not have been completed before the signature of the Grant Agreement (GA). The duration and the starting date of the action will be set out in the GA. The action shall have an indicative duration of three to five years; in any event, it shall be completed no later than 31 December 2033.

Budget

The Commission is considering a total budget of EUR 180 000 000 for the call for proposals.

The maximum EU contribution per funded project will not exceed EUR 30 000 000 allowing several proposals to be funded.

Depending on the number and quality of received proposals and the requested Union financial contributions, the Commission may decide to reallocate budget between calls.

The Commission is considering supporting specifically any optional work packages dedicated to the reinforcement of the physical and cyber protection of the industrial capacity targeted by the action, with a maximum EU contribution of EUR 500 000 per funded project.

Minimum financial size of the actions

The minimum financial size of the action to be eligible for funding is EUR 2 000 000.

Maximum number of legal entities forming part of the consortium

The number of legal entities forming part of the consortium shall not exceed 15 as per Article 34(3)(c) of the Regulation (EU) 2025/2643.

topicConditions:
General conditions

1. Admissibility Conditions: Proposal page limit and layout

described in Annex A and Annex E of the Horizon Europe Work Programme General Annexes.

Proposal page limits and layout: described in Part B of the Application Form available in the Submission System.

2. Eligible Countries

described in Annex B of the Work Programme General Annexes.

A number of non-EU/non-Associated Countries that are not automatically eligible for funding have made specific provisions for making funding available for their participants in Horizon Europe projects. See the information in the Horizon Europe Programme Guide.

3. Other Eligible Conditions

title: Advanced border surveillance and situational awareness
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Project results are expected to contribute to some or all of the following expected outcomes:

  • Improved detection, localization, characterization and, when applicable, neutralisation, of unmanned vehicles alone or in swarms, involved in trafficking or smuggling activities across external borders, while complying with legal and ethical guidelines;
  • Improved border situational awareness, especially in the context of large-scale movements of people across borders, including from potential instrumentalisation of irregular migration, conflicts, social, economic, environmental and climate stress;
  • Better safeguard and promotion of fundamental rights thanks to enhanced situational awareness;
  • Reliable, redundant detection and reaction capacities without putting staff and society at risk.

Scope:

Capabilities for situational awareness and surveillance of land and sea borders need improvement, in consideration of potential future challenges that may require updated capabilities. These challenges may include potential future large-scale movements of people across external borders, resulting from future attempts to instrumentalisation of irregular migration, but also from conflicts, social, economic, environmental and climate stress in the European neighbourhood; as well as increasing availability and capability of unmanned aerial, surface, and underwater vehicles with increased payload capacity and range that make it easier to transport goods and, possibly, persons, including in connection will illicit or illegal activities such as trafficking of goods and smuggling of people across external EU borders. These challenges will be particularly relevant in regions close to the European neighbourhood.

This may be particularly relevant for unsupervised and difficult-to-control land and sea borders of the Union and the Schengen area.

Research funded under this topic should develop solutions that, through better awareness, improve efficiency and reaction time of detection, search, rescue, and recovery operations near land and sea borders, in diverse geographical and meteorological conditions, taking into account the different and diverse needs. Research funded under this topic can also promote cross-border cooperation at European regional level around innovative border management solutions demonstration testbeds.

Actions funded under this topic should develop solutions that go beyond state-of-the-art in clearly demonstrable ways, including measurable improvements in detection range, accuracy, response time, automation, and system resilience.

Improved border surveillance and situational awareness must better safeguard and promote fundamental rights and EU values, with a particular regard to human rights, using an inclusive approach that addresses diverse needs. Solutions should also provide reliable and redundant capacities, while ensuring the safety of staff, users, and persons who may be victim of illicit activities across external borders.

The EBCG Capability Roadmap recognises that future capabilities that help detect cross-border irregularities and cases requiring Search and Rescue activities are essential. Solutions should be modular and scalable to cater to the regional and challenges specificities.

Compatibility and integration with the European Border Surveillance System (EUROSUR) is essential, and compatibility and/or exploitation of other European information-sharing environments, like the Common Information Sharing Environment (CISE), would be an additional asset.

Proposals should demonstrate that the proposed equipment and technologies contribute to cost reduction and energy efficiency of border surveillance and situational awareness operations.

Proposals submitted under this topic are expected to address the priorities of the European Border and Coast Guard (ECBG) and of its Agency (Frontex). This should start from the definition of requirements and the design phase, including alignment with the EBCG Capability Roadmap and on the engagement with the Agency during the project implementation. At the proposal preparation stage, Frontex will not provide guidance on or otherwise be involved in the preparation of project proposals. However, proposals should consider and anticipate that Frontex may observe pilots and demonstrations during project implementation to facilitate the future uptake of innovations within the border and coast guard community.

To ensure active involvement and timely feedback from relevant security practitioners, proposals should include a mid-term deliverable consisting of an assessment of the project’s mid-term outcomes, conducted by the practitioners involved in the project.

Technology Readiness Level - Technology readiness level expected from completed projects

Activities are expected to achieve TRL 6-7 by the end of the project – see General Annex B.

title: Accessible and available travel facilitation
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Project results are expected to contribute to some or all of the following expected outcomes:

  • Improved trusted, secure, and easier automated seamless facilitation for travel, border crossing through border crossing points (BCPs), and/or visa procedures with an integrated approach, minimized risk for bias, and accessible for all travellers minimising digital divides;
  • Facilitated solutions with same approach adaptable by all European border control staff, in all conditions and border control points (BCPs);
  • Reduced workload and improved safety, user experience and performance of practitioners’ staff involved in border management.

Scope:

Facilitation of travel and border crossings at border crossing points (BCPs) across the external EU borders went, and is further going, through developments thanks to updated procedures and regulatory frameworks and to innovative European technologies. From automated border control (ABC) gates to “no-gate” solutions and “seamless travel”, and with systems like the Entry-Exit System (EES), the Electronic Travel and Information Authorisation System (ETIAS), and the development of digital travel credentials and digital identity more in general, Europe has one of the most advanced, secure and facilitated border check systems in the world.

Travel facilitation schemes are still not as fair, inclusive and accessible as they should be. There are several technical exceptions that for example make difficult for families, other groups of people travelling together, people with disabilities and/or reduced mobility, or with relatively lower digital skills, to smoothly use travel and border crossing facilitation solutions. This is a capability gap of travel facilitation systems that has an impact on both a fair accessibility and availability for travellers, and on performance and efficiency of the systems themselves. Travel facilitation systems should ensure both security and easy passenger flow, while remaining accessible to all travellers.

On the other hand, both technical systems and procedures may have differences depending on the context or the BCP of application. This may be a limit for the performance and user experience of European integrated border management, especially in a perspective of a larger help to national members of the European Border and Coast Guard (EBCG) from the Standing Corps of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (EBCGA).

According to the EBCG Capability Roadmap, legal border crossings should be as swift and simple as possible, while at the same time allowing a smooth crossing of bona fide persons, and of the goods carried with them.

Innovation actions funded under this topic will develop and test solutions for advanced seamless travel and border crossing and/or visa procedures, protecting and promoting fundamental rights, minimising the risk for bias and being accessible for all travellers, with no or minimised limitations depending on age, sex, gender, disability, physical or digital abilities. To minimise potential for discrimination or physical or digital divide regarding travel facilitation schemes, solutions should be inclusive and accessible.

Furthermore, solutions should be tested for use with the same approach by all European border control staff in all conditions and BCPs.

The proposed solutions can include innovative technologies, innovative processes, innovative knowledge and/or a combination thereof. Solutions should include automated decision support systems suggesting to the end-users (border checks operators) which procedure, technology or database can be used without infringing rights of travellers. Solutions should also integrate and, if appropriate, further develop, biometric matching that minimises data shared (for example limiting to matching scores) to improve data protection.

Proposals submitted under this topic are expected to address the priorities of the European Border and Coast Guard and of its Agency (Frontex) and of the European Union Agency for the Operational Management of Large-Scale IT Systems in the Area of Freedom, Security and Justice (eu-LISA). This should start from the definition of requirements and the design phase of their work, including basing on the EBCG Capability Roadmap; and on the engagement with the Agencies during the implementation of the project. At the stage of proposal preparation, Frontex and eu-LISA will not provide any guidance on, or otherwise be involved in the preparation of, project proposals. Proposals should consider and foresee that Frontex and eu-LISA may observe pilots and demonstrations when the project will be implemented, with the aim of facilitating future uptake of innovations for the border, customs and coast guard community.

To ensure the active involvement of and timely feedback from relevant security practitioners, proposals should plan a mid-term deliverable consisting in the assessment of the project’s mid-term outcomes, performed by the practitioners involved in the project.

Depending on the particular scope of the proposal, participation of Customs Authorities is welcome.

Technology Readiness Level - Technology readiness level expected from completed projects

Activities are expected to achieve TRL 6-7 by the end of the project – see General Annex B.

Online Manual is your guide on the procedures from proposal submission to managing your grant.

Horizon Europe Programme Guide contains the detailed guidance to the structure, budget and political priorities of Horizon Europe.

Funding & Tenders Portal FAQ – find the answers to most frequently asked questions on submission of proposals, evaluation and grant management.

Research Enquiry Service – ask questions about any aspect of European research in general and the EU Research Framework Programmes in particular.

National Contact Points (NCPs) – get guidance, practical information and assistance on participation in Horizon Europe. There are also NCPs in many non-EU and non-associated countries (‘third-countries’).

Enterprise Europe Network – contact your EEN national contact for advice to businesses with special focus on SMEs. The support includes guidance on the EU research funding.

IT Helpdesk – contact the Funding & Tenders Portal IT helpdesk for questions such as forgotten passwords, access rights and roles, technical aspects of submission of proposals, etc.

European IPR Helpdesk assists you on intellectual property issues.

CEN-CENELEC Research Helpdesk and ETSI Research Helpdesk – the European Standards Organisations advise you how to tackle standardisation in your project proposal.

The European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for their recruitment – consult the general principles and requirements specifying the roles, responsibilities and entitlements of researchers, employers and funders of researchers.

Partner Search help you find a partner organisation for your proposal.

descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Project results are expected to contribute to some or all of the following expected outcomes:

  • Improved protection of minors, including by more reliable age assessments and by minimising the use of intrusive age assessment methods;
  • Improved adaptation, preparedness and cooperation of authorities in the fight against human trafficking;
  • Expanded European-based knowledge on reliability, accuracy and effectiveness of age assessment methods.

Scope:

Many unaccompanied children and young persons arriving at the external EU borders and seeking asylum, lack official documents showing their identity and age. Age assessment methods are important as they contribute to the determination of, for example, where an individual will be initially housed and what services, supports, and legal processes they will receive to ensure protection and, if applicable, child protection.

In other cases, minors are victim of trafficking of human beings (THB) criminal activities, either across the EU external borders, or within the EU borders. In other cases again, age assessment methods are necessary for law enforcement investigations on protecting children, forensic investigation, and/or the identification of victims.

No age assessment method can offer a 100% reliability. Different approaches have different sensitivity and specificity, and different sample sizes and representativeness, and some approaches are based on a non-European knowledge base. Furthermore, there is considerable variation in methods of age assessment. Methods may use approaches as diverse as interviews, psychological assessments and other holistic approaches; medical approaches such as X-rays, CT scans, DNA methylation, dental observation, or other analyses; other approaches such as image analysis; and they may use or not artificial intelligence (AI) for data analysis.

EU regulations, and guidelines by the European Union Asylum Agency (EUAA)[[EASO Age assessment practices in EU+ countries: updated findings (europa.eu) https://euaa.europa.eu/sites/default/files/EASO_Age_assessment_practices_updated.pdf[]], include safeguards and recommendations, such as that the least invasive methods should be used, and that medical methods should be used as a last resort. Further studies, reports or documents have also been elaborated by the European Migration Network[1], European networks of security practitioners for innovation, as well as at national level. The action funded by this topic should also consider these, as well as previous research, including but not limited to research by other relevant EU Framework Programmes projects.

This Coordination and Support Action should not develop methods or technologies of age assessment. Rather, it will analyse, including with practitioners, the current and potential methods for age assessment. It should assess and compare scientific reliability, sensitivity and specificity of different methods, as well as their potential risks for fundamental rights and how to minimize them.

While the research results would not imply any legislative or policy decision on age assessment methods, the research will develop evidence-based results on options for more (compared to the state-of-the-art) appropriate models of age assessment methods that protect fundamental rights, ensuring the use of an inclusive approach that addresses diverse needs. The results of research funded by this topic will contribute to capabilities for better identification of children and minors in the migratory, security, border management and other contexts, following the principles of the EU Strategy on the rights of the child[2]. They will also contribute to the exchange of practices among European authorities.

Synergies with other Horizon Europe Cluster 3 Destinations, such as “Better protect the EU and its citizens against Crime and Terrorism” and “Disaster-Resilient Society for Europe”, as well as with Destinations of Horizon Europe Cluster 2 “Inclusive Society”.

[1] https://ec.europa.eu/home-affairs/networks/european-migration-network-emn_en

[2] COM(2021) 142 final.
