beneficiaryAdministration:
Submit your proposal via our online form https://opportunities.getonepass.eu/opportunities/policy-enlarge before the relevant Cut-off Date.

Your application must be in English, and all mandatory sections must be completed.

Proposals cannot be modified after submission.

Multiple submissions for the same Funding Instrument and the same Cut-off Date are not permitted. If the same entity submits more than one proposal for the same Funding Instrument and Cut-off Date, only the most recently submitted proposal will be taken into consideration.

Each third party may benefit from no more than one POLICY ENLARGE Funding Instrument/Grant throughout the entire Open Call, irrespective of the Funding Instrument or Cut-off Date.

If the same third party is included in more than one proposal selected for funding, only the highest-scoring proposal involving that third party will be considered for funding. The other proposal(s) may be replaced by the next-ranked eligible proposal(s), in accordance with the ranking list.

If a third party has already received POLICY ENLARGE funding under a previous Cut-off Date, any subsequent proposal involving the same third party as a funded participant shall be considered ineligible for funding.

We will support up to 45 Projects in this Open Call:

  1. up to 15 projects under the Small Grants for Joint Regional Innovation Actions,
  2. up to 10 projects under the Small Grants for Collaborative Uptake of Results, and 
  3. up to 20 mobility grants under the Small Grants for People-to-People Cooperation Projects.

The total budget available for this Open Call is EUR 300,000.

POLICY ENLARGE expects to select an indicative number of proposals under each Cut-off Date (up to 4 under Funding Instrument #1, up to 3 under Funding Instrument #2, and up to 5 under Funding Instrument #3).

The project aims to select at least 1 Project per enlargement country. However, the final number of selected proposals, the distribution across countries, and the Cut-off Dates themselves may be flexibly adjusted based on the quantity and quality of applications and available budget. Any unused budget or places will be transferred to subsequent Cut-off Dates.
description:

callTitle: R&I Policy Support for Enlargement Countries
furtherInformation:
The following types of activities can be funded:

  1. Small grants supporting the development of collaborative R&I projects, accessing EU funding opportunities, strengthening R&I management and technology transfer capacities, and contributing to evidence-based policy reforms and digital and green transformation.
  2. Small Grants for Collaborative Uptake of Results: small grants aimed at implementing joint activities to support R&I, regulatory, or societal uptake of results.
  3. Small Grants for People-to-People Cooperation Projects: small grants aimed at implementing people-to-people cooperation projects with and within enlargement countries.

For Funding Instrument #1: Small Grants for Joint Regional Innovation Actions and Funding Instrument #2: Small Grants for Collaborative Uptake of Results: consortia including at least two independent legal entities, each established in a different enlargement country. The participating entities can be Companies, Research Organisations and Academia Research Groups, Non-profit entities, Digital Innovation Hubs /European Digital Innovation Hubs, and other relevant R&I actors.

For Funding Instrument #3: Small Grants for People-to-People Cooperation Projects: consortia including participation of Researchers, Artists, or Entrepreneurs - affiliated with independent legal entities, established either in different Enlargement Countries or in an Enlargement Country and an EU Member State.

Secondees, i.e. applicants for the mobility programme, must be citizens of an eligible enlargement country or hold a permanent residence permit in an enlargement country.

To be eligible, applicants shall be based in the Enlargement Countries, which are Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo*, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Türkiye, and Ukraine.

In the case of Funding Instrument #3: Small Grants for People-to-People Cooperation Projects, the hosting entity can also be from any EU Member State and its Overseas Countries and Territories (OCT) or Horizon Europe Associated Country.

POLICY ENLARGE partners and their affiliated entities can NOT be involved in the Financial Support to Third Parties recipients’ projects nor their employees and associates, including persons working under employment contract or contract equal or similar to employment contract and board members. Former employees and associates shall also be excluded if they were involved in the project execution at any stage.

Applicants under EU restrictive measures are ineligible:

  1. Following the Council Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/2506, as of 16 December 2022, no legal commitments can be signed with Hungarian public interest trusts established under Hungarian Act IX of 2021 or any entity they maintain.

Other restrictive measures:

  1. Since June 2024, the European Commission has suspended financial bilateral assistance directly benefiting Georgian authorities until further notice. As the EU continues to fund programmes directly benefiting Georgian citizens and has increased support to civil society and independent media, the project will support Georgian researchers. Regulation (EU) 2021/947, in particular Articles 3, 8, 19, 20, and 25 et seq., in conjunction with Financial Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 and the relevant Commission implementing decisions establishing or amending assistance programs for Georgia.

* This designation is without prejudice to positions on status and is in line with UNSCR 1244/1999 and the ICJ Opinion on the Kosovo declaration of independence

results.content: NACHIP - Second Open Call

beneficiaryAdministration:
About NACHIP

The NACHIP is an I3 project financed under the Interregional Innovation Investments call I3-2023-INV2a, which aims to accelerate innovation related to the North Adriatic Hydrogen Ecosystem (NAHV), with a focus on investments in hydrogen technologies. The goal is to strengthen the integration of hydrogen technologies into the ecosystem, boosting sustainability and enhancing the development of the hydrogen market. This project targets three main value chains (manufacturing, urban areas, and mobility) through five pilot actions:

1.Green hydrogen production from wave energy – Pag, Croatia

This pilot explores the production of green hydrogen with a novel technology that captures wave energy through a system of underwater devices installed beneath the sea surface. The pilot will also feature the application of multifunctional breakwater technology, being deployed for the first time in Europe.

2.Hydrogen use in urban Areas – Velenje, Slovenia

This pilot aims to establish a system for decentralized supply of energy from onsite renewables to be developed, operated and validated on a public building. The pilot focuses on integrating clean technologies through sector coupling (electricity, heat and hydrogen), supporting the transformation of the district heating system as coal is phased out (Just Transition).. Supporting activities will include the formation of a “local hydrogen alliance” pursuing the efficient utilization of renewable hydrogen within an environmentally sustainable and economically viable model.

3.Dynamic Hydrogen Releasers – Torviscosa, Italy

This pilot develops and demonstrates Dynamic Hydrogen Releasers (DHR), based on Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carrier (LOHC) technology. This innovation supports safe and efficient transport, storage, and on-demand release of hydrogen, contributing to Europe’s green mobility and industrial decarbonisation strategies. Throughout the development phase, this pilot needs to define the technical requirements and dimensions of the DHR units.

4.Cost-efficient hydrogen transportation cylinders – Udine, Italy

This pilot develops composite designs for cost-efficient hydrogen transportation cylinders. The focus is on improving vessel designs to enhance the mobility of energy storage, reducing costs while ensuring the safe and efficient transport of compressed hydrogen.

5.Gasification plant for waste materials – Zagreb, Croatia

This pilot focuses on developing a prototype gasification plant for waste materials. The universal gasification system is designed to process municipal solid waste (MSW) and convert it into valuable products such as synthesis gas (syngas) and charred residue (ash), which can be further used.

Objectives financial support to third parties (FSTP) in NACHIP

Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP), also referred to as cascade funding, is a mechanism of the European Commission designed to distribute public funding to either increase uptake of innovations on the side of recipients such as Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) or to support project implementation in addressing specific challenges and advancements towards key objectives.

Under NACHIP, FSTP enables targeted support to companies proposing hydrogen-based solutions at a TRL>7, connected to pilot projects that can be validated and deployed in real life settings. The mechanism ensures fast access to funding, reduced administrative burden and a competitive, transparent selection process.

The FSTP reinforces NACHIP demonstration activities through the following specific objectives:

  1. enabling market adoption of hydrogen-related technologies, products and services developed within Nachip’s pilots, combining different Key Enabling Technologies;
  2. fostering new technological solutions driven by SMEs.

More in particular, the FSTP under the NACHIP project will:

1.enable testing, validation and demonstration of hydrogen technologies in real-life environments through NACHIP pilot sites (specific to the NACHIP);

2.support TRL advancement of innovative solutions toward market readiness[1];

3.accelerate commercial deployment and exploitation of hydrogen innovations, including cross-border business opportunities;

4.address technical bottlenecks and integration challenges in the hydrogen value chain, completing the value chains of the companies belonging to the NACHIP consortium;

5.strengthen safety, standardization and regulatory compliance of hydrogen technologies;

6.promote cross-sectoral replication and interoperability to enable wider adoption across industries;

7.contribute to the investment portfolio and key performance indicators (KPIs) of the project.

Applicants can submit proposal through the NACHIP website https://www.nachip.eu

All applications must be filled and submitted in English language.

The evaluation is conducted by 3 experts. For evaluation process and criteri will be described in https://www.nachip.eu/open-calls/

For more information or assistance with the application process, participants can contact the NACHIP project directly:

nachip@meta-group.com

Questions to the above-mentioned email address can be submitted until 9th of October 2026.
description:
Activities that can be funded

Activities need to be coherent with EU priorities defined by the I3 call and must contribute to NACHIP objectives.

In line with the objectives of the I3 Programme, the Financial support in the NACHIP will be used for testing, validation, and demonstration of solutions in the field of hydrogen technologies and integration into real-world applications.

Three main areas of intervention have been identified for the sub-projects funded with the FSTP:

  1. Input: innovative chemicals/materials for the NACHIP pilot testing
  2. Process: solutions to optimize hydrogen-related processes used in the NACHIP pilots
  3. Output: applications of new technologies complementing the NACHIP value chains: mobility, urban, and manufacturing sectors

Sub-project proposed in these three main areas may focus on (non-exhaustive list):

  1. Prototype development: demonstrating the feasibility of proposed hydrogen technologies.
  2. Integration into existing infrastructure: scaling the technology for real-world applications.
  3. Innovation: novel solutions related to hydrogen energy storage, transport, or utilization.

A non-exhaustive list of potential activities that can be included in the sub-projects presented by the FSTP beneficiaries is reported in the following:

  1. trial and testing activities;
  2. market analysis linked;
  3. the acquisition and testing of materials;
  4. integration in the pilots of the SME’s solutions, demonstration in real/operational environment, small and/or medium scale;
  5. exploitation activities in new application sectors (cross-fertilisation);

Please to know better on activities that can be funded, check the Technical annex on the main web page.
